 Order

This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (corresponding to 482 of BNSS, 2023) for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No.29/2024 dated 29.01.2024, registered at Police Station - Ari, District -Seoni (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B,409,201 of IPC (now corresponding sections of BNS,2023),
section 66(C), 66(D) of I.T Act, 2000 and section 3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
Applicant apprehending his arrest in the aforesaid offence has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. As per the prosecution story, on 29.01.2024, S.D. Tantuvay, Sub Auditor/Administrator, Sewa Sahkari Samiti Takhlakala along with inquiry reports submitted an application stating that Satyanarayan Baghel is posted as Manager in the Sewa Sahkari Samiti and Abhishek Katre and Shobhachand Baghel are posted as Computer Operator and daily wages worker.
They all three hatched conspiracy and prepared forged document and illegally transported 7,400 quintal paddy worth Rs.1,61,54,200/- and paddy worth Rs.33,53,088/- was also found in deficit.
As such they have embezzled paddy of worth Rs.1,95,07,288/-.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
The only allegation against him is that he purchased paddy worth Rs.11,76,000/-.
It is contended that applicant was not aware of the fact that aforesaid paddy is stolen or has been brought from the society or is being illegally sold.

It is further contended that Kamal Rahangdale vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29062910/

sentences.text: He has already deposited Rs.11,35,160/- with the society.
He has no criminal background.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
5. Applicant is a bonafide purchaser or not is a question of fact which has to be decided only after recording of the evidence of witnesses.

Therefore, having taken into consideration the act attributed to the present applicant and the fact that he has already deposited the entire amount with the society but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant/accused may be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this anticipatory bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest applicant - Kamal Rahangdale be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.

(iv) In case, applicant is not arrested within a period of 10 days' by the Investigation Officer, he shall surrender himself before the Investigation Officer within 7 days' from today failing which this order shall become ineffective.
7.

However, it is being made clear that in case of bail jump and in violation of any of conditions imposed herein above, this order shall become ineffective and Investigation Officer/Trial Court shall be at liberty to proceed against the applicant as per law.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL Kamal Rahangdale vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29062910/
